how: Only what is open for you, oldest first. Each item says what to do, links everything it needs, and gives my recommendation. It leaves this page once you have answered it here or done it.

sections.name: Your rulings file is full (4,800 of 4,800 words), and your efficiency line is 118 words. Folding the old 1 November efficiency words and two dated phrases frees only about 25. May the cap rise by 100 words, to 4,900, for it?
sections.recommendation: Yes, to 4,900. The other way is to cut about 90 words of rulings still in force, which loses some of what binds. Your yes already stands either way; this is only about where it is written. No web link: the answer is this page.

sections.name: Your 22:19 choice, by the advisor: test Sonnet properly first. On Sunday, about 5 recent finished items are done again from the same starting point, once on Opus and once on Sonnet. A fresh Opus reviewer scores both blind, with tests, faults and cost counted. Tuesday's real day on Sonnet goes ahead only if Sonnet matches on 4 of 5 at clearly lower cost. Cap: about 3% of the week. Go ahead?
sections.recommendation: Yes. One change from the advisor's method: each run gets its own copy of the project on drive F, not a second working copy on C, which fills C and needs your yes to clean. No Unreal while the night's walk runs. No web link: the answer is this page.

sections.name: Ron and Darren dressed, as the game you play draws them (four pictures; tap one for full size). Short first: the knit reads smooth, one flat colour; Darren's neckband stands up stiffly with small peaks; Ron's collar has small bumps close up; no stitching on the jeans, no laces on the boots; hair at its default colour; the grey plate under Ron's boot is the street's iron cover, reading as a mat. No hole, no skin through the cloth, nothing modern. Do the clothes pass your look, judged on the clothes' floor?
sections.recommendation: Yes: they meet the clothes' floor (plain, 1990, no holes), which your rulings set for clothes instead of the 2026 bar. The shortfalls stay listed for when tailoring resumes. No web link: the answer is this page.
